findings.detail: Per-dispatch fan-out ceiling (Decision 6c, max-fanout-per-event default 50) is not in the user-spec. It is documented in User-Spec Deviations with reason ('fail-open /events rate-limit leaves public ingress unbounded during Redis outage') and marked [PENDING USER APPROVAL] in a draft spec. Per validation rules, documented scope creep with reason downgrades from scope_creep to documented_deviation. Draft status makes PENDING acceptable.
findings.recommendation: keep — justification is sound (closes a Redis-outage security hole at the API boundary); ensure user approves before spec promotion to approved

findings.detail: User-spec rate-limit text implies any auto-trigger counts (including tag-add from the UI panel). Tech-spec redefines 'auto-enroll' as 'depth > 0' (funnel-originated only), which exempts manual-UI tag-adds from the 20/min counter. This is a behavior difference, not merely a clarification. The deviation is documented in User-Spec Deviations with reason and marked [PENDING USER APPROVAL] in a draft spec — correctly handled. However the deviation entry characterises it as 'not a behavior change' which is slightly inaccurate; the actual behavior change is documented implicitly via the depth=0 rule.
findings.recommendation: adjust — amend the deviation entry wording: replace 'clarification of an internal ambiguity, not a behavior change' with 'reconciliation that excludes manual-UI tag/field writes from the volume counter (depth=0 rule); external api-event is also depth=0 and not counted — consistent with user-spec risk text treating external events as human/external roots'
